question.worked_solution:
Here, the denominator is the imaginary number $10\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+10\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-10\text{i},$ or simply $-10\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-10\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-7+6\text{i}}{10\text{i}} & =\frac{-7+6\text{i}}{10\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-10\text{i}}{-10\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{70\text{i}-60{\text{i}}^{2}}{-100{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{70\text{i}-60(-1)}{-100(-1)} \\  & =\frac{60+70\text{i}}{100}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{60+70\text{i}}{100} & =\frac{60}{100}+\frac{70}{100}\text{i} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}+\frac{7}{10}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
